name: CHAS Card Eligibility and Subsidies: Green vs Orange vs Blue Explained
content:
CHAS Card Eligibility and Subsidies: Green vs Orange vs Blue Explained

Quick Answer

  • CHAS tiers are determined by per-person household monthly income or, if there's no income, the Annual Value (AV) of your home.
  • CHAS Blue: household monthly income per person of $1,500 and below, or residence AV of $21,000 and below.
  • CHAS Orange: household monthly income per person between $1,501–$2,300, or AV between $21,001–$31,000.
  • CHAS Green: household monthly income per person above $2,300, or AV above $31,000.
  • CHAS Green cardholders receive no subsidy for common illnesses (like cough or cold) — only chronic condition subsidies.
  • Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation cardholders receive enhanced subsidies above all three standard tiers.
  • CHAS subsidies apply only at participating private GP and dental clinics — not polyclinics.

Introduction

Many Singapore residents carry a CHAS card without fully understanding which tier they're in or what it actually covers — and that gap in understanding directly costs money at the clinic counter. The confusion is understandable: eligibility depends on a "per-person household income" calculation that few residents have ever manually worked out, and the subsidy tables differ significantly depending on whether you're being treated for a common illness or a chronic condition.

This guide breaks down exactly how CHAS eligibility is calculated, what each tier (Blue, Orange, Green) actually pays for, and how Pioneer and Merdeka Generation status changes the picture.

How CHAS Eligibility Is Determined

CHAS tiers are assigned based on one of two calculations:

  1. Household monthly income per person — your total household income divided by the number of household members.
  2. Annual Value (AV) of your residence — used only if the household has no income (e.g., retirees without income sources).
Tier Household Monthly Income (Per Person) Residence AV (If No Income)
CHAS Blue $1,500 and below $21,000 and below
CHAS Orange $1,501 – $2,300 $21,001 – $31,000
CHAS Green Above $2,300 Above $31,000

What Each Tier Actually Covers

Common Illnesses (e.g., cough, cold, minor infections)

Tier Subsidy Per Visit
CHAS Green Not applicable — no subsidy
CHAS Orange Up to $10
CHAS Blue Up to $18.50
Merdeka Generation Up to $23.50
Pioneer Generation Up to $28.50

Selected Simple Chronic Conditions

Tier Subsidy Per Visit Annual Cap
CHAS Green Up to $28 $112/year
CHAS Orange Up to $50 $200/year
CHAS Blue Up to $80 $320/year
Merdeka Generation Up to $85 $340/year
Pioneer Generation Up to $90 $360/year

Selected Complex Chronic Conditions

Tier Subsidy Per Visit Annual Cap
CHAS Green Up to $40 $160/year
CHAS Orange Up to $80 $320/year
CHAS Blue Up to $125 $500/year
Merdeka Generation Up to $130 $520/year
Pioneer Generation Up to $135 $540/year

The Detail Most Residents Miss: CHAS Green Gets No Common Illness Subsidy

A frequent surprise for CHAS Green cardholders is discovering, at the clinic counter, that their card provides zero subsidy for a routine cough-and-cold visit — CHAS Green only applies to chronic condition management, not acute common illnesses. This is worth checking before assuming any CHAS card automatically reduces every GP bill.

Worked Example: Comparing a Family's CHAS Tiers

The Wong family has three generations living together: grandparents (Pioneer Generation), parents (working adults), and children (students).

  • Grandparents: Hold Pioneer Generation cards, receiving the highest subsidy tier — up to $28.50 for common illness visits and up to $90/visit (capped $360/year) for simple chronic conditions such as diabetes management.
  • Parents: With a combined household income divided by household size resulting in a per-person income of $2,600/month, they fall into CHAS Green — meaning they get chronic condition subsidies but nothing for a common cold visit.
  • Children: As dependants under the same household income calculation, they would also fall under CHAS Green, receiving chronic condition coverage only, not routine illness subsidies.

This example shows why understanding your specific tier matters — the grandparents' visits are heavily subsidised, while the working parents effectively pay full price for common illness GP visits despite holding a CHAS card.

Comparison Table: CHAS Blue vs Orange vs Green

Feature CHAS Blue CHAS Orange CHAS Green
Income threshold (per person) $1,500 and below $1,501–$2,300 Above $2,300
Common illness subsidy Up to $18.50 Up to $10 None
Simple chronic condition subsidy Up to $80/visit, $320/yr cap Up to $50/visit, $200/yr cap Up to $28/visit, $112/yr cap
Complex chronic condition subsidy Up to $125/visit, $500/yr cap Up to $80/visit, $320/yr cap Up to $40/visit, $160/yr cap
Best for Lower-income households Middle-income households Higher-income households (chronic care only)

Step-by-Step: Checking and Applying for Your CHAS Tier

  1. Log in to the CHAS website or HealthHub using your Singpass account.
  2. Check your current registered tier (Blue, Orange, or Green) under your health profile.
  3. If your household income has changed significantly, you can apply or reapply for reassessment through the same portal.
  4. Confirm your participating GP or dental clinic accepts CHAS before your visit — not all clinics participate.
  5. Present your CHAS card or digital CHAS record (via Singpass) at the point of payment.

Common Mistakes

  • Assuming any CHAS card covers common illness visits. CHAS Green cardholders receive no subsidy for cough-and-cold type visits — only for chronic condition management.
  • Visiting a polyclinic and expecting CHAS to apply. CHAS subsidies are only valid at participating private GP and dental clinics, not polyclinics.
  • Not recalculating per-person income after a life change. A change in household size (e.g., a child moving out, a parent passing away, or a new dependant) can shift your per-person income calculation and change your tier.
  • Overlooking Pioneer/Merdeka Generation enhancements. Eligible seniors sometimes don't realise their generational status entitles them to a higher subsidy tier than standard CHAS Blue.
  • Not confirming clinic participation before treatment. Always check that your chosen GP or dental clinic is a CHAS-participating provider before assuming a subsidy will apply.

Frequently Asked Questions

How is my CHAS tier determined? By your household's monthly income divided by the number of household members (per-person income), or by your residence's Annual Value if the household has no income.

Does CHAS Green cover a common cold visit? No — CHAS Green cardholders do not receive subsidies for common illnesses, only for selected chronic conditions.

Can I use CHAS at a polyclinic? No — CHAS subsidies apply only at participating private GP and dental clinics, not polyclinics, which use a separate subsidy structure.

How much more do Pioneer Generation cardholders get compared to CHAS Blue? Pioneer Generation cardholders receive up to $28.50 for common illness visits (versus $18.50 for CHAS Blue) and higher chronic condition subsidies with higher annual caps.

Can my CHAS tier change over time? Yes — if your household income or composition changes, you can apply for reassessment, which may move you into a different tier.

What's the difference between CHAS Orange and CHAS Blue? CHAS Orange applies to households with per-person income between $1,501–$2,300; CHAS Blue applies to $1,500 and below. Blue cardholders receive higher subsidy amounts across all condition categories.

Is there an annual cap on CHAS chronic condition subsidies? Yes — each tier has a specific annual cap per chronic condition category (simple vs complex), ranging from $112/year (CHAS Green, simple) up to $540/year (Pioneer Generation, complex).

How do I check which CHAS tier I currently hold? Log in to the CHAS website or HealthHub with your Singpass account to view your current registered tier.

Key Takeaways

  • CHAS eligibility depends on per-person household income or residence Annual Value if there's no income.
  • CHAS Green cardholders get no common illness subsidy — only chronic condition coverage.
  • Pioneer and Merdeka Generation cardholders receive enhanced subsidies above all standard CHAS tiers.
  • CHAS only applies at participating private GP and dental clinics, never polyclinics.
  • Check and update your CHAS tier whenever your household income or composition changes significantly.
